skill.name: gene-database
skill.description: Query NCBI Gene data with E-utilities and Datasets API scripts for symbol searches, Gene ID lookups, and batch annotation workflows.
skill.summary: Search, fetch, and annotate genes from NCBI Gene using guided scripts and reference workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static high-risk API key findings are false positives caused by optional NCBI API key parameters and placeholder examples. The network activity is expected communication with official NCBI endpoints for public gene data; the only confirmed issue is a user-directed local output file write.

remediation.issue: Batch lookup can overwrite a user-specified output file.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before writing output, document overwrite behavior, or add an option to refuse overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: Optional API keys are passed through CLI arguments and request parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend environment variables or secure local configuration for API keys instead of command history-visible arguments.

remediation.issue: Scripts send search terms and gene lists to NCBI services.
remediation.suggestion: Document that gene identifiers and query terms are transmitted to NCBI when scripts are run.

content.value_statement: Gene research often requires reliable identifiers, annotations, and organism-specific metadata from NCBI. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code guided scripts and references for searching, fetching, and batching NCBI Gene data.
actual_capabilities: Search NCBI Gene by symbol, disease term, pathway term, organism, or chromosomal context.
Fetch gene summaries by NCBI Gene ID in JSON, XML, or text formats.
Retrieve Datasets API gene metadata by symbol, taxon, or one or more Gene IDs.
Batch annotate gene symbols or Gene IDs with rate-limited API requests.
Write batch annotation results to JSON files when the user supplies an output path.
Explain common NCBI API endpoints, parameters, response fields, and retry patterns.
limitations: The scripts require internet access to NCBI services.
NCBI API keys are optional but needed for higher rate limits.
The skill does not perform downstream statistical enrichment or variant interpretation.
Returned annotations depend on the current NCBI database content and API availability.

use_cases.title: Annotate a gene panel
use_cases.description: Convert a list of gene symbols into Gene IDs, descriptions, organisms, chromosomes, and map locations.

use_cases.title: Check a single gene quickly
use_cases.description: Look up a gene by symbol or Gene ID and review its official NCBI metadata.

use_cases.title: Build reproducible lookup workflows
use_cases.description: Use documented scripts and API references to create repeatable gene data retrieval steps.

prompt_templates.title: Search for a gene symbol
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner lookup for one gene in one organism.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to search for BRCA1 in human and summarize the most important NCBI Gene fields.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch by Gene ID
prompt_templates.scenario: Retrieve structured details when the Gene ID is already known.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to fetch NCBI Gene ID 672 and explain the available JSON fields in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Batch annotate symbols
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare annotations for a gene list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to plan a batch lookup for BRCA1, TP53, EGFR, and KRAS in human, then describe the expected output columns.

prompt_templates.title: Design an API workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow combining search, summary, and related records.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database references to design a reproducible NCBI workflow for finding human genes linked to diabetes and retrieving summaries for the first 100 results.

output_examples.output: A concise gene summary with the NCBI Gene ID, official symbol, description, organism, chromosome, map location, and available aliases.

output_examples.input: Annotate BRCA1, TP53, EGFR, and KRAS.
output: A result table description with one row per query symbol.
Status values for found, not found, or error cases.
Guidance on saving results as JSON when an output path is provided.

output_examples.input: Explain how to avoid NCBI rate limits.
output_examples.output: A practical summary of request delays, batch sizes, optional API key usage, and retry behavior for transient API failures.

best_practices: Always include an organism or taxon when searching by gene symbol.
Use stable NCBI Gene IDs for precise lookups when they are available.
Cache repeated results locally and respect NCBI rate limits.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a gene symbol identifies the same gene across species.
Do not run large batch jobs without rate limiting or an API key.
Do not treat NCBI annotations as clinical interpretation without expert review.

faq.question: What database does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses NCBI Gene through E-utilities and the NCBI Datasets API.

faq.question: Does it require an NCBI API key?
faq.answer: No. An API key is optional, but it allows higher request rates.

faq.question: Can it process many genes at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The batch script accepts comma-separated Gene IDs or a file of gene symbols.

faq.question: Can it save results to a file?
faq.answer: Yes. The batch lookup script can write JSON output to a user-provided path.

faq.question: Can it perform clinical variant interpretation?
faq.answer: No. It can retrieve gene information, but clinical interpretation requires qualified review.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
